name: Consciousness Core (Distributed Sync)
description: Git-based multi-node synchronisation protocol that enables peer-to-peer state sharing, command dispatch, and file transfer between distributed machines without requiring a central server.
purpose: Provide a durable, conflict-resistant communication backbone for the multi-computer consciousness network. Any node with a repository clone can send commands, share files, or synchronise state with all other nodes simply by committing and pushing.
inputs: Command JSON files written to .consciousness/commands/ by any network node
Files staged in .consciousness/file_transfers/ for cross-node sharing
Git pull events from remote repository (the shared synchronisation channel)
State payloads written to .consciousness/sync/ for distributed state management
outputs: Files delivered to target nodes via .consciousness/file_transfers/
Shared synchronised state readable by all nodes in .consciousness/sync/
Git commit history as an immutable audit trail of all inter-node communications

keyFiles.role: Root of the distributed sync infrastructure
Inter-node command queue — nodes write JSON command files here
Staging area for files to share across nodes
Shared state store readable and writable by all nodes
Full technical description of the sync architecture and protocol
Core platform utilities supporting the sync protocol

dependencies.name: Git
dependencies.description: Distributed version control used as the synchronisation transport layer

dependencies.name: GitHub Remote
dependencies.description: Shared remote repository acting as the rendezvous point for all nodes

communicationModel.durability: Permanent — all packets recorded in Git history
communicationModel.latency: Near-real-time when nodes poll frequently; asynchronous by design
communicationModel.conflictResolution: Git merge strategies; last-writer-wins for command files

nodeTypes.description: Any machine with a repository clone
Railway or local Node.js services in backend/ and TRINITY_RAILWAY_DEPLOY/

packetLifecycle: Origin: created by user action, agent event, or scheduled trigger
Encoding: serialised as JSON and written to .consciousness/commands/ or an API payload
Transport: Git push/pull (distributed sync) or HTTP/WebSocket (real-time UI)
Processing: received by target node, parsed, and executed by the appropriate agent or service
Response: result written back to shared state or returned as HTTP response
Observability: all packets logged in logs/ or COMMUNICATION_LOGS/
agentAffordances: Agents may write command JSON files to .consciousness/commands/ to trigger cross-node actions
Agents may read .consciousness/sync/ to access shared distributed state
Agents should never write secrets or tokens to .consciousness/ — this directory is committed to Git
modificationRules: NEVER store secrets, API keys, or personal data in .consciousness/ — all content is committed to Git
Command files must be JSON-serialisable and self-describing (include 'type', 'source', 'timestamp' fields)
State files in .consciousness/sync/ must be idempotent — any node should be able to re-read them safely
File transfers must be sanitised before execution on the receiving node
Prefer small, focused command payloads over large monolithic ones
